title: Kouign-Amann

ingredientGroups.title: Dough
items: 2 Tbsp European-style butter (30 g), melted and cooled, plus more for bowl
3 cups all-purpose flour (400 g), plus more for dusting

ingredientGroups.title: Butter block
items: 12 oz chilled unsalted European-style butter (340 g)

steps: Butter a large bowl. Dissolve yeast in ¼ cup very warm water at 110–115° and let stand about 5 minutes, until foamy. Add sugar, salt, flour, melted butter and cold water; mix to a shaggy dough. Knead about 5 minutes, until soft and slightly tacky.

Place in the buttered bowl, cover and rise until doubled, 1–1½ hours. Punch down, knead lightly, cover and chill until doubled again, 45–60 minutes. Pat into a 6 × 6-inch square, wrap and freeze until very firm but not frozen, 30–35 minutes.
Beat butter-block ingredients on low about 3 minutes until uniform. Shape between parchment into a 12 × 6-inch rectangle ¼ inch thick, wrap and chill 25–30 minutes until firm but pliable.
Roll dough into a 19 × 7-inch rectangle. Place butter over the upper two-thirds; fold the lower third over the butter, then the upper third down. Seal the edges.

Rotate 90° counterclockwise, opening on the right. Roll to 24 × 8 inches, about ⅜ inch thick; fold in thirds. Wrap and freeze about 30 minutes until firm but not frozen, then refrigerate about 1 hour.

With the opening on the right, roll to 24 × 8 inches and fold in thirds. Rotate 90° counterclockwise and roll again to 24 × 8 inches. Sprinkle with 2 Tbsp sugar and fold in thirds. Wrap, freeze about 30 minutes, then refrigerate about 1 hour.

Roll slightly larger than 16 × 12 inches, trim to size and cut into 12 squares. Coat two 6-cup jumbo muffin pans with spray. Sprinkle the squares with ¼ cup sugar, press, turn and repeat with another ¼ cup. Fold corners to the center and place in muffin cups.

Cover and refrigerate 8–12 hours. Preheat oven to 375°. Sprinkle cold pastries with the remaining 2 Tbsp sugar and bake 25–30 minutes, until golden and deeply caramelized. Remove immediately to a rack and cool.
reviewFlags: The source gives 110–115° for the yeast water and 375° for baking without specifying a temperature scale. Confirm the scale before cooking.
